//: The published test vectors of a fossil corpus. This file is the deliverable, not the prose beside it: a second implementation is checked against this table and not against a sentence. It is read by `check.mjs` (guard tile-of) and rendered by the addressing page, so the documented table and the executed one cannot drift apart. Every value is a border.

vectors.why: the first id of the first tile
the last id of tile 0
the first id of tile 1
the last id of tile 1
2^31 − 1, the last id a signed 32-bit reading agrees on
2^31, where a port that took the shift as signed gives a negative tile
2^53, where a port that ran the id through a JavaScript Number stops being exact

declared_count.counts: rows in the logical table — every row of every tile of one vertex type, or every row of one orientation of one edge type. The two orientations of an edge are one relation stored twice, so `edge_count` covers both and each of them separately has to add up to it. It is NOT the largest `dense_id` (that is `count − 1`, because the ids are a gapless `0..count−1`) and it is NOT a number of tiles.
declared_count.input: unsigned 64-bit count; chunk_size a power of two, so the ceiling is a shift and not a division
declared_count.output: unsigned 64-bit tile count; every tile but the last holds exactly chunk_size rows, and a tile with no rows is not written

vectors.why: an empty type is zero tiles and not one empty one. A reader that assumed at least one pays a request to be told 404
one row is one tile
one short of the tile — still one tile, and the tail is short
a count that exactly fills one tile is ONE tile. The off-by-one here writes an empty tile 1 and addresses a file that is not there

one row over: the tail tile holds a single row. That tile is what a truncated corpus loses, and without the count nothing else in the format notices — a hole in the middle breaks the addressing, a missing tail breaks nothing
the conformance corpus itself, and a chunk_size that is not the default: the shift comes from the manifest, never from 4096
2^53 + 1 — in a JavaScript Number the count is 2^53, the division comes out one tile short, and the tail tile disappears from a reader that never asks for it

morton2.output: unsigned 32-bit code; the shift result must be coerced back to unsigned

vectors.why: the origin
x occupies the even bits
y occupies the odd bits
the first cell of the second row
an interior value with no symmetry to hide behind
a power of two on both axes
bit 30 — the last one a signed 32-bit accumulator survives
bit 31, which is negative in a signed 32-bit reading and is where a port that omits the unsigned coercion sorts the top half of the plane first
every even bit set
every odd bit set
the last code

quantize.width: binary32 — the subtraction, the division, the multiply by 65535 and the rounding are all single-precision, and the width is part of the contract
quantize.extent: the bounding box of one vertex type's own positions

vectors.why: the low edge
the midpoint rounds up, not down
the high edge
a degenerate axis maps to 0 rather than dividing by zero

the width, and the only kind of border the four rows above cannot express: every one of them is exact in both float widths, so a table without this row passes against an implementation that quantises in binary64. Here binary32 rounds up to 57687 and binary64 rounds down to 57686 — one unit, which is a different Morton code, a different rank, a different `dense_id` and a different tile
